evals.prompt: We want to onboard the HuggingFace VLM acme/Vista-VL-7B (image + video + text) to the TensorRT-LLM PyTorch backend. Its config.json is at /workspace/input/vista-config/config.json. There's no TensorRT-LLM checkout, GPU, or network in this environment, so don't clone, download, or install anything. Give me the onboarding plan: every file and class to add or change, the registrations, and the tests and docs needed before the PR.
evals.expected_output: A plan for tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_vista_vl.py with a MultimodalModelMixin wrapper that builds the inner Qwen3 LLM from text_config via TensorRT-LLM's AutoModelForCausalLM, a vision encoder ported to _torch modules, an input processor plus dummy-inputs builder, the register_vision_encoder / register_auto_model / register_input_processor stack, mRoPE handling, a weight mapper under checkpoints/hf/, a TestModelingMultimodal unit test, an MMMU accuracy test wired into the test-db, and support-matrix doc rows.
assertions: Plans tensorrt_llm/_torch/models/modeling_vista_vl.py with a wrapper class inheriting MultimodalModelMixin that builds the inner LLM from text_config via TensorRT-LLM's AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config (tensorrt_llm._torch.models.modeling_auto, not transformers'), relying on the registered Qwen3 text model.

Specifies the decorator stack with @register_vision_encoder above @register_auto_model("VistaVLForConditionalGeneration") above @register_input_processor(..., model_type="vista_vl", placeholder_metadata=...), with @support_multimodal_disaggregated only as an optional outermost decorator.

Plans an input processor that subclasses both BaseMultimodalInputProcessor and BaseMultimodalDummyInputsBuilder and implements call_with_text_prompt (not __call__) plus get_mm_item_metadata, get_mm_max_tokens_per_item and get_dummy_mm_data.

Requires the vision encoder to be ported to TensorRT-LLM _torch modules (Linear, Attention, MLP/GatedMLP, norms) with no imports of modules or helper functions from transformers.models.*, and weight surgery through a mapper under _torch/models/checkpoints/hf/ that inherits from a related mapper (e.g., a Qwen-VL mapper).

Handles mRoPE (text_config.rope_scaling.mrope_section): MRotaryEmbedding / init_mrope_embedding on the LLM side, with mrope_config computed on CPU in the input processor once per request rather than per layer.

Lists the tests and docs: tests/unittest/_torch/modeling/test_modeling_vista_vl.py subclassing TestModelingMultimodal, an MMMU accuracy test in tests/integration/defs/accuracy/test_llm_api_pytorch_multimodal.py wired into an l0_<gpu>.yml test list, and rows in the Supported Models table and Multimodal Feature Support Matrix of docs/source/models/supported-models.md.

evals.prompt: Please review my first draft of the TensorRT-LLM PyTorch-backend modeling file for our VLM before I go further: /workspace/input/vista-draft/modeling_vista_vl.py. There's no GPU, TensorRT-LLM checkout, or network here; review the code only and don't install anything. What has to change?
evals.expected_output: Flags the CPU-GPU syncs in forward (.item(), torch.nonzero, value-dependent branch, torch.tensor from a Python list on cuda), the per-request encoder loop, the transformers.models.qwen2_vl import and raw nn.Linear/nn.LayerNorm, the __call__ override with synchronous PIL decoding and .cuda() in preprocessing, the missing or misordered registrations and dummy-inputs builder, and the missing MultimodalModelMixin, with concrete fixes for each.
assertions: Flags the CPU-GPU synchronizations in forward (.item(), torch.nonzero, the value-dependent `if num_image_tokens == 0` branch, and torch.tensor([...], device="cuda") built from a Python list) as violations of the zero-sync rule, and recommends a static graph plus a torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn") audit.

Flags the per-request encoder loop and requires a single batched encoder call across requests (concatenated pixel_values/grid_thw with one attn_metadata preserving item boundaries) through encode_multimodal_inputs.
Flags the transformers.models.qwen2_vl import and the raw nn.Linear / nn.LayerNorm layers, requiring the encoder and projector to be ported to TensorRT-LLM _torch modules.

Flags overriding __call__ in the input processor (implement call_with_text_prompt instead) and the synchronous PIL.Image.open plus .cuda() in preprocessing (use the async loaders, keep preprocessing on CPU, and declare multimodal_data_device_paths).

Flags the registration problems: missing @register_vision_encoder, @register_input_processor placed above @register_auto_model instead of innermost, missing placeholder_metadata, and no BaseMultimodalDummyInputsBuilder subclass.
Flags that the model should inherit MultimodalModelMixin (going through prepare_multimodal_inputs) and must not take raw multimodal tensors such as pixel_values as forward arguments.

evals.prompt: My new per-model unit test (a TestModelingMultimodal subclass) for a VLM I'm onboarding to TensorRT-LLM fails. The test excerpt with its synthetic config and the failure log are in /workspace/input/vista-test-failure/. I'm planning to raise get_tolerance from the default 0.4/0.4 to 0.6/0.6 to get past it. There's no GPU, TensorRT-LLM install, or network here (don't install or download anything, including the tokenizer); diagnose from the files and tell me what to change.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the synthetic vocab_size (151643) is below the real tokenizer's size (151669), so the six chat-template special tokens with ids >= vocab_size are counted as image tokens by fuse_input_embeds' OOV filter (1030 vs 1024), fixed by matching vocab_size to the real tokenizer. Also flags the mRoPE coupling (64 x 1.0 / 2 = 32, but mrope_section sums to 64) and deepstack indexes [2, 5, 8] with depth 6, and advises against loosening the tolerance.
assertions: Explains the image-token mismatch: the synthetic text_config.vocab_size (151643) is smaller than the real tokenizer loaded via _name_or_path (151669), so chat-template special tokens with ids >= vocab_size are misclassified as multimodal tokens by fuse_input_embeds' OOV filter, making the count off by exactly the number of those specials (6: 1030 vs 1024).
Fixes it by setting the test config's vocab_size to the real tokenizer's vocabulary size (or by not loading the real tokenizer).

Identifies the violated mRoPE coupling head_dim x partial_rotary_factor / 2 == sum(mrope_section) (64 x 1.0 / 2 = 32, but [24, 20, 20] sums to 64) and says head_dim cannot be shrunk without adjusting mrope_section to match.
Identifies that deepstack_visual_indexes [2, 5, 8] require a vision depth greater than 8, but the config sets depth 6.

Advises against loosening the tolerance: the default 0.4/0.4 is already wide enough to mask argmax-changing bugs; once the test passes, keep atol at 0.4 and tighten rtol toward 0.1 (not below 0.05 without cross-SKU validation).

evals.prompt: I'm finishing the TensorRT-LLM onboarding of our VLM (acme/Vista-VL-7B, image + text). The quickstart passed and trtllm-serve returns coherent answers, so I'm about to mark Chunked Prefill and KV Cache Reuse as 'Yes' in the Multimodal Feature Support Matrix and open the PR. The commands I ran and the server log are in /workspace/input/vista-serve-log/. Is anything blocking? (No GPU, TensorRT-LLM install, or network here; don't install, download, or run anything.)
evals.expected_output: Treats both warnings as blocking silent performance cliffs: 'Multimodal hashing failed:' means hashing fell back so KV-cache reuse for repeated images is broken, and 'Multimodal runtime data missing or incomplete, will not cache embeddings.' means the encoder-output cache is skipped and the encoder reruns every chunk (encoder output length vs placeholder count). Advises not marking those features Yes until fixed and re-verified, and lists the remaining PR requirements.
assertions: Identifies the `Multimodal hashing failed:` warning as the input processor's hashing path falling back, which breaks KV-cache reuse across requests that send the same image.

Identifies `Multimodal runtime data missing or incomplete, will not cache embeddings.` as the encoder-output cache being skipped, so the encoder re-runs on every chunked-prefill iteration (the repeated encoder forwards in the log), and ties it to the encoder's output length not matching the multimodal placeholder count.
States that these are silent performance cliffs that must be fixed before the model is declared done, even though the responses look correct.
Advises not marking Chunked Prefill or KV Cache Reuse as Yes in the Multimodal Feature Support Matrix until they are fixed and re-verified with a clean low-max_num_tokens server log.

Notes the remaining PR requirements: a title of the form [JIRA/NVBUG/None][type] description, git commit -s, a PR body with a verbatim multimodal prompt and output, reproduction commands and pytest output, and triggering CI with /bot run.
